title: MoEZip: Routing-Aware KV Cache Compression for Sparse Mixture-of-Experts LLMs
summary: MoEZip replaces routing-agnostic KV eviction methods (e.g., attention-score-only policies) with a scoring system that combines attention weights and a Fisher-information metric of routing sensitivity, so eviction preserves expert selection during generation. The cost is additional per-token scoring computation, implementation complexity beyond standard eviction policies, and applicability restricted to sparse MoE architectures rather than dense models. It can fail if the Fisher-based sensitivity estimate does not transfer to a given MoE model or task, if the serving stack does not expose per-layer routing distributions needed to compute the metric, or if retention ratios below the evaluated regime degrade quality sharply.
rationale: The method is relevant only if the reader self-hosts MoE models with long-context workloads on the 24 GB GPU; API-based usage cannot apply KV eviction, so adoption requires workload-specific validation against existing eviction baselines.
technique: Routing-aware KV cache eviction for MoE models

claims.statement: MoEZip replaces routing-agnostic KV eviction methods (e.g., attention-score-only policies) with a scoring system that combines attention weights and a Fisher-information metric of routing sensitivity, so eviction preserves expert selection during generation. The cost is additional per-token scoring computation, implementation complexity beyond standard eviction policies, and applicability restricted to sparse MoE architectures rather than dense models. It can fail if the Fisher-based sensitivity estimate does not transfer to a given MoE model or task, if the serving stack does not expose per-layer routing distributions needed to compute the metric, or if retention ratios below the evaluated regime degrade quality sharply.
At 10% KV retention, MoEZip improves over the SoTA baseline by +24 and +20 points on average on LongBench and RULER, corresponding to 2.3x and 4.9x higher scores respectively.
